headline: A day after BI's hike the 1Y reprices 8.9bp higher and the 5Y adds 2.6bp, while the 10Y edges to a new high of 7.739% even as Treasuries rally 3bp; JISDOR sets a record 18,269 and the daily flow signal is −0.73
summary: PHEI's IGSYC caught up with BI's hike at the front: the 1Y rose 8.9bp to 6.798% after barely moving on Wednesday, the 2Y was flat at 7.029% (+0.1bp) and the 3Y slipped 0.7bp to 7.252%, while the belly kept cheapening, the 5Y up 2.6bp to 7.576% (+10.7bp this week) and the 7Y 2.4bp to 7.700%. The 10Y rose 1.0bp to 7.739%, the highest on the dashboard's history since Nov 2021, and the 15–30Y 0.4bp to 7.743%. 2s5s widened 2.6bp to 54.8bp, the widest of 16 stored days, and the 2s5s10s fly rose 4.3bp to 38.5bp, while 1s2s fell 8.9bp to 23.0bp and the 1Y now sits 79.8bp over the 6.00% BI-Rate. FR0109 rallied 2.9bp to 7.528% (3.6bp cheap, from 8.4bp) and PBS040 2.4bp to 7.528% (7.2bp cheap); the fitted PBS 5Y is on the curve (0.1bp through), retail 14.5bp rich at 5Y, and AAA 3Y 48.5bp over, the narrowest of 15 stored days.
drivers: The front end priced the hike a day late; the belly kept selling

After a 1.1bp dip on decision day, the 1Y rose 8.9bp to 6.798% and the 1Y−BI-Rate gap widened back to 79.8bp, still the 12th percentile of 16 stored days (average 103.6bp). Reuters-cited analysts see BI tightening into 2027, and Governor Destry Damayanti said today that global rates will stay higher for longer; the 4–7Y rose 1.4–2.6bp and 2s5s hit 54.8bp, which reads as the market pricing more than one further hike. The 3Y slipped 0.7bp, so the move was concentrated at 1Y and 5–7Y.
The rupiah gave back the hike bounce

JISDOR fixed 0.09% weaker at a record 18,269 and spot closed 0.12% weaker at 18,254 while most Asian currencies firmed (Kontan, Bloomberg data); BI's hike has not yet put a floor under the currency. Commentators pointed to hawkish Fed talk (Governor Waller floated a 50bp December hike) and US–Iran tension. JISDOR is 0.72% weaker this month and the 20-session USD/IDR change is +1.83%, which keeps the rupiah part of the flow signal bond-bearish.
Treasuries rallied again; INDOGBs did not follow

The US 10Y fell about 3–4.5bp on Wednesday to 5.06–5.07% on lower oil, despite hawkish FOMC minutes in which almost all officials saw further hikes as likely. At the 1-year daily beta of 0.28 that implies −0.8bp for the INDOGB 10Y; it rose 1.0bp, so Treasuries explain none of today's move, the third session running. The INDOGB − UST spread widened to 266.9bp from 262.9bp (85th percentile of 52 weeks, range 191–286bp), a nominal pick-up before currency risk.
Stocks fell a fourth day; foreigners sold equities, not (per BI) bonds

The JCI lost 1.02% to 5,194.14, with foreign net selling of Rp563.6bn across the market (Kontan). BI's Destry put the year-to-date foreign equity outflow at Rp81.6tn against Rp143tn of inflows into SBN and SRBI, and Kontan cites Rp43tn of foreign SBN inflow to Nov 11; that does not rule out bond selling since, and who traded bonds today is not published. Over 20 sessions the JCI is down 12.5%, the equity part of the signal's most bearish input after the 10Y trend.

BI-Rate 6.00%, +25bp; DF 5.25%, LF 6.75% (f split: 10 of 27 for a hike, rest hold; p 5.75%)

Almost all saw further hikes as likely; a couple open to >25bp in Dec (f hawkish lean, p held 3.75–4.00%, 10–2)
Treasuries still rallied 3–4.5bp on oil; no pass-through to INDOGBs.

Firm core spending; Treasuries rallied ~2bp into the close.

Portfolio +$4.8bn; equities −$0.9bn (f n/a, p n/a)
Inflows led by global bond/sukuk issuance and SBN; equities still leaking.
SBSN auction (Nov 17)
Bids Rp20.10tn, awarded Rp10tn; SPNS Rp6.90tn of it, PBS041 at 7.09% (f target Rp10tn, p bids Rp28.56tn)
Demand skewed to short bills; long PBS bids were selective.
Budget through October (Nov 13)
Deficit 1.47% of GDP (f n/a, p 1.24% through Sep)
On track, but Rp164tn of Q4 auction issuance is still to come (Kontan).
SUN auction (Nov 10)
Bids Rp79.71tn (p Rp31.09tn); awarded Rp35tn vs Rp30tn target; FR0110 7.44%, FR0111 7.68%
Strong demand at higher yields; the next SUN book is the first test after the hike.
view: The hike has not turned the rupiah, and the curve is pricing more: the 1Y caught up, 2s5s is the widest stored at 54.8bp and the 10Y at 7.739% is 1.1bp under my 7.75% underweight trigger with Treasuries again no help. The daily Bond Flow Signal is −0.73 (sell-off; −0.88 yesterday on today's rebuild): the 10Y trend part is the most bearish (z +1.77, +52.8bp over 20 sessions), then the JCI (z −1.21, −12.5%) and the rupiah (z +0.65, +1.83%), while the spread, 20.0bp above its 130-day average (z +0.70), leans bond-bullish; the sell-off episode runs from Sep 28 (29 sessions, +53.1bp). Since July 2022 the daily signal scores a Sharpe of 0.80 outright (201.6bp) and 0.86 hedged against Treasuries (210.2bp), against −45.0bp for holding the 10Y, but sell-off calls were right only 52.3% of the time over the next 20 sessions (hedged 51.9%; rally calls 57.9%, hedged 64.8%) and the 10Y rose just 0.1bp on average after them; on the same daily build the outright Sharpe was 1.01 in Jul 2022–Aug 2024 and 0.66 since. The weekly build scores 0.57 and 0.75; a variant using the US 10Y trend reaches 0.92 and 0.95 on the weekly build but was chosen after the fact and is not live, and all of these are in-sample back-tests. Over four weeks the INDOGB 10Y is up 28.1bp and the US 10Y 11bp, yet at the weekly beta of −0.13 the Treasury-linked part is −1.4bp and +29.5bp is residual, the part Treasuries do not explain. I stay neutral on the 10Y in a 7.60–7.85% range, keep the 5Y as the curve trade (buy FR0109 at 7.60–7.70%, now 7.2bp away after its rally), and treat the 1–2Y as the bucket most exposed to a December hike.

buckets.name: Front end 1–2Y vs BI-Rate
buckets.why: The 1Y rose 8.9bp to 6.798%, so the gap over the 6.00% BI-Rate widened to 79.8bp from 70.9bp, still the 12th percentile of 16 stored days (average 103.6bp); the 2Y is 7.029%, 102.9bp over. The 3M (0.25Y) is 6.27% and the 1M 6.16%, 16bp over the policy rate. The 7.00% add level was not reached (1Y 20bp away); no position. Wednesday's flat 1Y proved a lag rather than a verdict.
buckets.call: Neutral. Add 1–2Y at 1Y 7.00%, target 6.75%, stop 7.25%; unchanged, since the 1Y is still well inside its stored average gap to the policy rate.

buckets.name: Belly 5Y (FR0109 / PBS040)
buckets.why: The IGSYC 5Y rose 2.6bp to 7.576% (81st percentile of 16 stored days, average 7.502%), +10.7bp this week, and the 2s5s10s fly rose 4.3bp to 38.5bp (88th percentile, average 27.0bp). FR0109 bucked it, rallying 2.9bp to 7.528% and richening to 3.6bp cheap from 8.4bp, so the entry (7.60–7.70%) moved 7.2bp away and is not filled.
buckets.call: Keep: buy FR0109 at 7.60–7.70%; target 7.35%, stop 7.95%. The curve point is cheap; the bond needs to cheapen back to it.

buckets.name: 10Y outright
buckets.why: The IGSYC 10Y rose 1.0bp to 7.739%, a fresh top of the stored history since Nov 2021 (100th percentile of 1,124 days, average 6.79%), against a 3bp US rally; +11.1bp this month. The signal is −0.73, but the underweight rule also needs a 10Y close above 7.75%, 1.1bp away, so it is not triggered. FR0108 rose 1.1bp to 7.736%, on the curve.
buckets.call: Neutral, range 7.60–7.85%. Underweight if the signal stays below −0.5 and the 10Y closes above 7.75%; tactical long only above 7.85% (stop 8.05%) or once the signal is above 0 with JISDOR below 18,000.

buckets.name: 10s20s curve (FR0108 vs FR0107)
buckets.why: IGSYC 10s20s is 0.4bp (38th percentile of 16 stored days, average 1.3bp, range 0.1–2.9bp); the long end is flat. The benchmark spread FR0107 − FR0108 is 0.7bp (from 0.2bp), 5.7bp from the −5bp re-entry.
buckets.call: Wait. Re-enter the FR0108/FR0107 steepener duration-weighted at −5bp or lower, target +5bp, stop −12bp.

buckets.name: PBS sukuk vs FR
buckets.why: The fitted PBS 5Y is 0.1bp through IGSYC (73rd percentile of 15 stored days, average −1.4bp); the fit rests on four series (level −8.8bp, slope 23.8bp), so confidence is limited. PBS034 rallied 4.4bp to 7.639% and is 5.3bp rich; on the benchmark-history measure its richness rose 4.9bp, another loss for the FR-over-PBS034 switch, with the switch-back (PBS034 5bp cheap) 10.3bp away. PBS040, held from 7.52%, is 7.528%, 0.9bp against, and 7.2bp cheap to the curve; PBS030 lost 13.1bp to 7.006% with the front end.
buckets.call: Hold PBS040 from 7.52%: target 7.30%, stop 7.80%. Hold FR over PBS034 but add a stop (new, after two losing days): close if PBS034 is more than 10bp rich to IGSYC; switch back once it is 5bp cheap.

buckets.name: Corporate credit (AAA 3Y)
buckets.why: PHEI's AAA 3Y slipped 0.8bp to 7.737%, in line with IGSYC, so the spread is 48.5bp, the narrowest of 15 stored days (7th percentile, average 50.0bp). AA is 90.3bp over, the widest stored (average 86.9bp), A 151.9bp and BBB 223.1bp over AA (13th percentile, average 236.6bp). Fifteen days is a thin base and PHEI's corporate curves track IGSYC almost one-for-one; the add level (AAA 3Y past 70bp) was not reached.
buckets.call: Hold AAA/AA; add only if AAA 3Y widens past 70bp. Avoid BBB while funding costs rise with the BI-Rate.

buckets.name: Retail SBN 5Y (ORI/SR)
buckets.why: The fitted retail curve is 14.5bp through IGSYC at 5Y (40th percentile of 15 stored days, average −13.5bp) and 5.5bp over at 2Y; the fit uses 25 series with a 75bp slope, so part of this is fit artefact. Secondary spreads run from 52bp rich (SR024T3) to 61bp cheap (ORI027T3, 7.635%); ORI026T6 is 7.681%, 34bp over. ST017 (open to Dec 2) floors at 6.95% (2Y) and 7.05% (4Y), below the IGSYC 2Y (7.03%).
buckets.call: New money: FR0109 or PBS040 for liquidity; ST017 for hold-to-maturity buyers who want further BI-hike upside. Buy secondary retail only at the cheap end (ORI026T6, ~34bp over).

igs:10.note: +1.0bp to 7.74%, a new high, vs −0.8bp UST-implied

watch: Next: US weekly jobless claims tonight (Thu Nov 19), Indonesia's Q3 balance of payments (Fri Nov 20; current-account deficit seen at $3.3bn from $12.5bn), the next SUN auction as the first test of demand after the hike, MSCI changes after the Nov 30 close, the ST017 book closing Dec 2, the Fed decision on Dec 9 and FTSE deletions on Dec 21; a 10Y close above 7.75% would trigger the underweight, while JISDOR back below 18,000 would argue against a December BI hike.
